standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of a surjection from a finite free module onto any module, and the lifting of a map into a tensor product along it

standard_prerequisites.name: A module is projective if and only if it is a direct summand of a free module

standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the factorisation found in the diagram into finite projectivity.

core_obligations: Write the two duality identities expressing that the unit and counit compositions are the identity (proof lines 18432-18434).
Choose a finite free module mapping onto M and lift the unit to a map from the ring into the tensor product with the dual (proof lines 18434-18440).
Draw the resulting commutative diagram and deduce that the identity of M factors through the free module, so that M is a direct summand and hence finite projective (proof lines 18440-18456).
Identify the dual with the module of homomorphisms into the ring through the displayed map and compute the evaluation, which are the remaining assertions (proof lines 18456-18458).
proof_roadmap: Lift the unit along a free cover (proof lines 18434-18440).
Chase the diagram to get the splitting (proof lines 18440-18456).
Identify the dual and compute the evaluation (proof lines 18456-18459).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a module with a left dual in the monoidal category of modules is finite projective, identifies the dual with the module of homomorphisms into the ring and computes the evaluation in terms of that identification, and the proof is a 28-line argument built on a lifting of the unit of the duality. It writes the two duality identities, lifts the unit along a map from a finite free module onto the given module, draws the resulting commutative diagram and reads off from it a factorisation of the identity of the given module through the finite free module, which exhibits it as a direct summand and hence projective; the same diagram then gives the identification of the dual with the Hom module and the formula for the evaluation. The lifting step and the diagram chase that produces the splitting are the substance, and both are displayed.
